propositions: The MCP and reconciler surface blocks in the AC1 equivalence contract were trivially passing by re-calling the shared composer with identical arguments instead of driving the actual entry points, preventing detection of parity bugs if those surfaces stopped routing through the composer

The contract must drive the real MCP entry point via build_server() and call_tool(), and the real reconciler entry point via rebar_reconciler.__main__.main() with argv, capturing their actual composed snapshots rather than re-invoking the composer

Each surface's captured snapshot must be asserted against absolute expected content (repo root, envelope version, config keys with distinct provenance) in addition to cross-surface comparison, because comparing only equal-to-each-other is vacuous when perturbing the composer moves all surfaces together

The capture mechanism must use module-global rebinding of rebar._operation_config.compose_operation_snapshot at call time rather than import time, so that emit_shadow_snapshot's dynamic name resolution genuinely reaches code entered through the real surfaces
The contract must fail explicitly when a surface no longer routes through the composer, detected by assertion on an empty capture list rather than silent passage of an empty comparison

Shared input must move from cli_overrides to project layer (sync.push) and env layer (REBAR_VERIFY_MAX_TICKET_DESCRIPTION_CHARS) because MCP and reconciler entry points pass no cli_overrides, while the CLI block retains its own cli-layer provenance assertion
